//: Blindfold for whole-rendering-layer authoring. Launch with:  claude --settings .claude/ui-blind.settings.json
//2: Supersedes skin-blind.settings.json for the /build-ui flow. Blocks every rendering of the CURRENT visual language while leaving the behaviour contract, the rendering boundary, the skin API, the non-drawing services and the test fixtures readable. See .claude/commands/build-ui.md and UI-RENDERING-BOUNDARY.md.
//3: Difference from skin-blind: Skins/Bracket is also blocked. It is an abandoned attempt that reproduced the incumbent arrangement in a new palette; reading it re-transmits exactly the failure /build-ui exists to prevent.
//4: The Bash text-tool denials are broad on purpose. Read/Grep denials alone do not stop `sed -n '1,80p' Theme.swift` from reconstructing a blocked file. Nothing legitimate requires reading a blocked path: UI-RENDERING-BOUNDARY.md carries every contract the agent needs.
//5: Services/ and Models/ are deliberately NOT blocked. The key router, focus manager, cooldown gate and request/response models must be read — they hold no pixels, and DialogKeyRouter in particular must be reproduced call-for-call by the new chassis wrapper.
//6: Images stay blanket-denied, which means the agent CANNOT read screenshots written inside the repo. capture-states.sh therefore must write outside it — pass OUTDIR=<scratchpad>/shots. This is the one setup detail that silently breaks the see-your-work loop if missed.
//7: screencapture is deliberately NOT denied: the agent must screenshot every state of its own layer. The rule that keeps that honest is behavioural — capture only the window id returned by test-cases/capture-dialog.swift, and never run a dialog without DIALOG_SKIN set to the new layer's id.
